correction.text: Quan Prefecture and Zhang Prefecture, the Qingyuan Circuit (renamed Pinghai in 964)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The pages give Quan and Zhang prefectures and no area; Quanzhou and Zhangzhou 60 km circles (about 24,000 km2) are the researcher's reading. Liu Congxiao expelled the rebel Lin Zanyao from Zhang Prefecture in the fall of 946.

ledger.note: 946: Liu Congxiao takes Quan. In spring 946 'Liu took command of Quan's army from Wang Jixun'; the Southern Tang's Li Jing then made him prefect of Quan, and in spring 947 he pressed the Southern Tang detachment out of Quan. The circuit was created in 949.
946: Zhang Prefecture is cleared. 'Liu expelled the rebel Lin Zanyao from Zhang Prefecture' in the fall; Dong took over Zhang.

949: the Qingyuan Circuit is created. 'Li Jing created the Qingyuan Circuit, based at Quan, and made Liu its jiedushi'; Liu stayed loyal to the Southern Tang in 958 and sent tribute to the Song in 960.

963: Chen Hongjin takes over. In summer 963 he went to Zhang Hansi's headquarters and Zhang yielded his seal; he reported to Li Yu (who commissioned him) and secretly asked the Song to accept his submission (accepted; 964).
964: Song names the Pinghai Circuit. 'In 964 Emperor Taizu commissioned him military governor and renamed the circuit Pinghai.'

region.text: Pinghai Circuit: Quan and Zhang prefectures

ledger.note: 978: Chen Hongjin surrenders Quan and Zhang. 'Chen went to Kaifeng and surrendered Pinghai Circuit, consisting of Quan and Zhang prefectures, to Emperor Taizong' (the article text gives 977, its infobox reign ends 978); his surrender helped persuade Qian Chu to submit Wuyue.

wars.name: Southern Tang pressure on Quan
wars.outcome: The Southern Tang left Quan in spring 947 after Liu Congxiao pressed its detachment; no border changed.
wars.note: The Liu Congxiao page gives no battle for Quan itself.

certainty.note: Two prefectures with no frontier line on either page.

sources.title: Liu Congxiao
sources.note: Quan and Zhang 944-947, the 949 circuit, tribute to Later Zhou, Song and Southern Tang.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks it; its 946 Min-gap shape of ea-04-c's note covers the area); requested by the min, wuyue, southern-tang and southern-chu dossiers. Open points: (1) no English page titled Qingyuan Circuit was opened (wikipedia null); (2) Chen Hongjin's surrender is 977 in the text and 978 in the infobox; (3) the Southern Tang dossier lacks a Qingyuan vassal pair although Li Jing 'created' the circuit in 949 and Chen Hongjin was commissioned by Li Yu in 963 while secretly submitting to the Song in 963-964; (4) the south of Fujian between 945 and 946 (Wang Jixun's Quan) is not detailed; (5) wars is empty: no page names a war.
